findings: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp: extending CanDoPerfectHashJoin to JoinType::RIGHT is a general change. It uses only the join type, the condition shape, the integer key type, a structural range cap (2^22) and a density guard (count >= range/4). Nothing refers to names, literals or row counts.

NULL build keys are handled: TemplatedFillSelectionVectorBuild now skips invalid keys, so for RIGHT joins (has_null=false, NULL-key rows kept) they never get a slot. They are still emitted by ScanFullOuter because their found-match flag starts false when rows are appended (join_hashtable.cpp:415).

The dup check change (Count() > range+1) is only an early bail-out. Exact duplicate detection still happens through bitmap_build_idx in the build fill. For RIGHT joins Count() includes NULL-key rows, which only makes the check more conservative.

Slots are only marked matched when they hold a build row: the probe selects only slots that are valid in the bitmap (or all slots when dense), so the uninitialised entries in build_row_locations are never dereferenced.

Parallel probe threads write the matched byte unsynchronised, but always with the value 1. This is the same harmless race the regular HT has on its found-match flag. MarkMatchedBuildRows runs once in PrepareScanHT, after all probing and before the outer scan.
Spilling joins reset perfect_join_executor; FULL, SEMI and ANTI joins are still excluded; enabling compute_aggregates_anyway for RIGHT joins only adds a cheap build min/max.
